clue.text: He may take steps to execute certain measures

definitions.text: He may take steps to execute certain measures

parts.words: He may take steps to execute certain measures
parts.note: steps suggests action taken to put policy measures into effect, but the steps are footwork and the measures are bars of music, as in a waltz or a reel

explanation.definitionFit: A person who performs footwork in time to music literally takes steps to the bars of a tune.

clue.text: Two articles about the Commanding Officer's tropical snake

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as printed: 'Two articles about the Commanding Officer's tropical snake (8)'. AN + A + CO gives ANACO, but no clue word accounts for the remaining NDA; no parse found.
annotationWithheld.clue: Two articles about the Commanding Officer's tropical snake

clue.text: Interpret study as half-genuine

parts.note: to con is an old word for to study or learn by heart

indicators.note: half of the two-letter word as is taken, here its second letter

parts.note: genuine means true, as in a true friend

explanation.surface: Someone is told to treat a piece of research as only partly authentic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half-genuine' looks like one hyphenated idea, but 'half' works on 'as' (giving S) while 'genuine' supplies a separate word.
explanation.definitionFit: To construe something is to put a particular meaning on it, to understand it a certain way.

clue.text: Able to recall things about wine I've accumulated

parts.note: re is the Latin-derived word for about or concerning, as in business letters
tent is an old name for a deep red Spanish wine used in communion
the contraction I've written without its apostrophe

explanation.surface: A wine buff can still remember everything they have stockpiled in the cellar.
explanation.walkthrough: TENT is a dark red Spanish wine, an old crossword favourite. 'accumulated' simply links the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A retentive memory holds on to facts and experiences well.

clue.text: Tolerated boy endlessly seen around Scouts rally

indicators.note: seen around means the shortened name is placed round the other piece
endlessly means the name loses its final letter

parts.note: James is a boy's name
bore, the past tense of bear, means put up with or tolerated

explanation.surface: A lad who was put up with is spotted at a large youth gathering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' drops the last letter of the boy's name, and 'seen around' means the shortened name wraps round the word for tolerated. 'Scouts' is part of the definition, not a separate piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A jamboree is the large international gathering of Boy Scouts and Girl Guides.

clue.text: Versatile businessman known for his knavery?

definitions.text: Versatile businessman known for his knavery?

parts.words: Versatile businessman known for his knavery?
parts.note: a knave in a pack of cards is the jack, and a businessman deals in many lines of trade, so this is a card-playing image of someone who turns their hand to everything

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes a handy person who can do many kinds of work, competent in each though master of none.

clue.text: Army unit ordered to capture oil installation

indicators.note: to capture means one piece holds the other inside it

parts.note: bade, the past tense of bid, means ordered or commanded
a rig is an oil-drilling installation, on land or at sea

explanation.surface: Soldiers are commanded to seize an oil platform.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ordered' looks like an anagram signal, but it is the past tense of bid; 'to capture' tells you that word holds the oil installation.
explanation.definitionFit: A brigade is a military formation made up of several battalions or regiments.

clue.text: Harsh time to obtain dietary fibre

parts.note: harsh means rough, as in a rough voice or rough treatment
an age is a long period of time

explanation.surface: A severe period comes along, so it is time to eat more bran.
explanation.definitionFit: Roughage is the indigestible plant matter in food that aids digestion.

clue.text: An outstanding contribution to a snail's good looks!

definitions.text: An outstanding contribution to a snail's good looks!

parts.words: An outstanding contribution to a snail's good looks!
parts.note: outstanding means literally sticking out, and good looks means the ability to see well, not beauty: the organ in question is the stalk that carries a snail's eye

explanation.definitionFit: A snail's eyes sit on top of long movable stalks that protrude from its head.

clue.text: Tape is sometimes so attractive

definitions.meaning: audio and video tape is coated with an iron-oxide layer that records signals magnetically
attractive in the physical sense of drawing iron towards itself

explanation.surface: Recording tape can sometimes be alluring.
explanation.definitionFit: Recording tape stores sound on a magnetised coating, and a magnet pulls iron objects towards it.

clue.text: Tiny amphibian owned by this compiler, say?

indicators.note: say means the words are spoken aloud to give a word that sounds the same

parts.note: a newt is a small amphibian; one owned by the setter, who speaks of themselves as this compiler, would be my newt

explanation.surface: The setter is showing off a very small pet salamander.
explanation.walkthrough: Spoken as one word, 'my newt' sounds like the adjective meaning very small, pronounced my-NEWT.
explanation.definitionFit: Something minute is extremely small, almost too small to see.

clue.text: Fee paid by a stock buyer to learn music

definitions.text: Fee paid by a stock buyer

parts.note: to con is an old word meaning to learn or study
a tango is a piece of Argentine dance music

explanation.surface: A stockbroker's client pays a fee to take dance lessons.
explanation.walkthrough: On the old London Stock Exchange, a buyer who deferred paying until the next settlement day paid a charge to the seller under this name.
explanation.definitionFit: In finance, this is the premium a buyer pays a seller to put off settling a deal.

clue.text: Way to limit pain? It's in the bag

indicators.note: to limit means the outer letters surround and hold in the other piece

parts.note: St is the abbreviation for street, a way
an ache is a dull pain

explanation.surface: Someone seeks a way to keep pain down and finds the answer packed away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It's in the bag' sounds like 'success is certain' but describes a small packet, such as a scented one tucked inside a handbag.
explanation.definitionFit: A sachet is a small sealed packet, of scent, sugar or shampoo, often carried in a bag.

clue.text: Shell a Continental state held by evil characters

parts.note: un is French for a, the indefinite article

indicators.note: held by means one piece sits inside the other
characters means the letters of the word next to it are used in a new order

parts.note: the word evil supplies its letters
VA is the abbreviation for the US state of Virginia

explanation.surface: A European country is seized by wicked people, and someone shells it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'characters' means the letters of 'evil' are rearranged, and 'held by' places the state abbreviation among them, after the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A univalve is a mollusc, such as a snail, with a one-piece shell, so the word also names that kind of shell.

clue.text: Irritating new tax that's dividing you from the French

indicators.note: dividing means one piece splits the other in two by going inside it

parts.note: vous is French for you

indicators.note: new means the letters that follow are made into a new arrangement

parts.note: the word tax supplies its letters
i.e., short for id est, means that is

explanation.surface: A new tax that puts a wall between you and the French is annoying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges the letters of 'tax' plus the abbreviation for that is, and 'dividing' splits the French word after its first letter to take them in.
explanation.definitionFit: Vexatious means causing annoyance or distress, as in a vexatious lawsuit.

clue.text: Front spaces for trebles

definitions.meaning: a front, as in the frontage of a building or a bold front
on the treble stave, the four spaces between the lines are the notes F, A, C and E, which music pupils learn as a word

explanation.surface: Seats at the front are kept for three-fold bets.
explanation.definitionFit: A building's frontage is its facade, and the four spaces of the treble staff, read upwards, spell the word.

clue.text: Pigs half cooked in this vessel

indicators.note: cooked means the letters are mixed, as in cooking the books

parts.note: the word pigs supplies its letters
the word half supplies its letters, not a halving

explanation.surface: Half-cooked pork is served in a particular dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half' looks like an instruction to take half of 'Pigs', but it is fodder: 'cooked' rearranges all eight letters of PIGS HALF.
explanation.definitionFit: A flagship is the lead vessel of a fleet, carrying the admiral's flag.

clue.text: Monocular giants producing work in recurrent series

indicators.note: in means one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: cycles are series of events that recur
op, short for opus, is a work in music

explanation.surface: One-eyed giants produce their work in repeating series.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth these were a race of giants, each with one eye in the middle of the forehead.

clue.text: Kiss hastily and have a nibble

definitions.meaning: to give a quick, light kiss on the cheek

explanation.surface: Someone gives a quick kiss and then takes a little bite.
explanation.definitionFit: A brief perfunctory kiss and a bird's light strike at food share the same verb.

clue.text: Show curiosity about least uncommon old instrument

indicators.note: about means one piece goes round the other

parts.note: to pry is to be nosy, to show curiosity

indicators.note: uncommon means the letters are taken in an unusual order

parts.note: the word least supplies its letters

explanation.surface: Someone is nosy about an old instrument that is rarely seen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uncommon' rearranges the letters of 'least', and 'about' puts the word for nosiness round them, its first letter before and its last two after.
explanation.definitionFit: A psaltery is an ancient stringed instrument, plucked like a zither.

clue.text: One at the wheel giving firm kiss to lover

parts.note: Co is the abbreviation for company, a firm
X is the conventional sign for a kiss at the end of a letter
a swain is an old poetic word for a lover or suitor

explanation.surface: A driver gives their sweetheart a firm kiss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One at the wheel' suggests a driver, but here it is the person steering a boat.
explanation.definitionFit: A coxswain steers a rowing boat or ship, so is at its helm.

clue.text: Involuntary responses of a Welshman having cable installed

indicators.note: installed means one piece is fitted inside the other

parts.note: Rees is a common Welsh surname, standing for any man from Wales
flex is the flexible electric cable on an appliance

explanation.surface: A man from Wales has his electrical wiring put in and twitches in reply.
explanation.walkthrough: FLEX is the British word for an appliance's electric cord.
explanation.definitionFit: Reflexes are automatic reactions, like the knee jerk, made without conscious thought.

clue.text: Creature only existing originally in three rivers?

indicators.note: in means those letters are put inside the other pieces

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for river, used twice, and the Dee is a river in Wales, England and Scotland
the Dee is a river in Wales, England and Scotland
R is the abbreviation for river

indicators.note: originally means the first letters of the words next to it are taken

explanation.surface: A creature that exists only where three rivers meet.
explanation.walkthrough: The three rivers are R, DEE and R; 'originally' gives O and E from 'only existing', which go inside, after the first R.
explanation.definitionFit: The roe deer is a small European deer, a woodland animal.

clue.text: Move right out of corridor into the kitchen

indicators.note: move out of means that letter is removed from the word

parts.note: a gallery is a long passage or corridor

explanation.surface: Someone shifts from a passageway into the cookhouse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Move ... out of' together tell you to take R from GALLERY.
explanation.definitionFit: A galley is the kitchen on a ship or aircraft.

clue.text: Unpitying woman? Not so

parts.note: Ruth is a woman's name
less means not so much, as in less kind

explanation.surface: A woman is asked if she is merciless, and denies it.
explanation.walkthrough: Ruth is also an old word for pity, so the answer literally means pity-less.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruthless means showing no pity or compassion.

clue.text: Joiner employed in cabinet-making

parts.note: a joiner sounds like a carpenter making cabinets, but it is the punctuation mark joining the two words cabinet and making in the clue itself

explanation.definitionFit: This short dash links words into a compound, as in the clue's own two-part word.

clue.text: Bishop once said to be unorthodox

indicators.note: unorthodox means not following the usual order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the word once supplies its letters
the word said supplies its letters

explanation.surface: A church leader was formerly reported to hold heretical views.
explanation.definitionFit: As a noun, a diocesan is a bishop in charge of a diocese.

clue.text: Father's attempts at making cakes

parts.note: pa is a word for father, with the possessive s
tries are attempts

explanation.surface: Dad has a go at baking.
explanation.definitionFit: Pastries are small baked goods made with pastry, like cakes or tarts.

clue.text: Possibly saw a youth leader entertain outside

indicators.note: outside means one piece goes round the other

parts.note: to sing is to entertain an audience

indicators.note: leader means the first letter of the word youth is taken

explanation.surface: Perhaps someone saw a group leader of young people performing out of doors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'saw' looks like a verb but is the noun, an old proverb. 'outside' puts SING round A and Y.
explanation.definitionFit: A saw is an old proverb or maxim, one kind of familiar expression.
